quizzes.production_note: Needs partial-credit matching. Source any real stage-crew terminology from a drama educator before launch. Key only explicit stated requirements or intended effects in the supplied brief; interpretive taste judgments remain unscored and may have multiple valid answers.

quizzes.title: Surprise Party Timeline
quizzes.hook: Order the secret steps of a fictional surprise party so decoys, deliveries and arrivals all line up.
rounds: 4 timelines: order five steps with clues
4 problems: choose the fix that keeps the secret
quizzes.seed: The cake arrives at 5, the guest of honor returns at 6. Order: hide cake, dim lights, send decoy text, everyone arrives.
quizzes.payoff: Operation score with raw points and a note on which timing clue each step satisfied.
quizzes.audience: Friend groups, roommates and family organizers
quizzes.production_note: Uses existing order and choice controls. Author clues; verify any customs reference with cultural reviewers. Keep fictional guests.

quizzes.title: Roommate Treaty Table
quizzes.hook: Draft house rules for a fictional shared apartment and see what trade-offs your group settles on.
rounds: 5 conflicts: choose a rule
3 trades: pick what to give up
2 final clauses: order what matters most
quizzes.seed: Guests visit often and one roommate works nights. Choose a rule: quiet hours, a guest calendar or a shared notice board.
quizzes.payoff: Treaty card of your rules with a playful pair, Flexible Hosts vs Quiet Keepers. Not about real roommates.
quizzes.audience: Roommates and students, solo or passing one device
quizzes.production_note: Uses choice and order controls. Scenarios are fictional. Review for housing-type diversity and avoid implying one norm. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. One shared group response per task; no private participant state or individual compatibility scoring.

quizzes.title: Spot the Unspoken Assumption
quizzes.hook: Rescue a fictional group conversation by finding the one missing detail that prevents everyone from understanding the same plan.
rounds: 4 fictional exchanges: identify the unstated date, place or responsibility
4 reply choices: select the message containing every explicitly required detail
quizzes.seed: A message says “meet Friday at six,” but the friends are in two time zones. Which missing detail prevents a shared clock time?
quizzes.payoff: Eight communication repairs with the missing assumptions revealed; no judgment of real friendships.
quizzes.audience: Anyone who hosts or attends small gatherings
quizzes.production_note: Use closed fictional exchanges and stated communication goals. Accept equivalent complete replies; do not score politeness or personality.

quizzes.title: Pass the Plot Pen
quizzes.hook: Each player picks the next story beat for a shared tale, and the ending changes with the group.
rounds: 4 branch points: choose the next story beat
3 twists: pick how the group reacts
1 ending: choose the final line
quizzes.seed: The map leads to a locked greenhouse. Next beat: climb the roof, find the key under a pot or knock on the door.
quizzes.payoff: Story recap of your chosen path with its ending title; a keepsake, not a score.
quizzes.audience: Game-night groups and classrooms
quizzes.production_note: Needs branching journey tooling. Author all branches and endings in-house; test every path for tone. No real-person data.

quizzes.title: Five-Minute Group Quest
quizzes.hook: A pass-the-phone mini adventure the group can finish in one short break.
rounds: 4 quick forks: choose a path together
3 puzzles: solve a clue as a team
quizzes.seed: A lantern flickers at the fork. Light it, leave it, or follow the sound? Each choice changes the next clue.
quizzes.payoff: Quest card showing your route and clues solved, with a short ending note.
quizzes.audience: Short-break groups, commuters and classrooms
quizzes.production_note: Needs branching journey tooling. R10 shows only broad gaming participation, not quiz demand. Author and playtest all routes.

quizzes.title: Spot It Together
quizzes.hook: Find hidden clues in a busy illustrated party scene, each person tapping what the others missed.
rounds: 4 scenes: tap clue hotspots
4 questions: choose what the clues reveal
quizzes.seed: In the picnic scene, tap the two objects that suggest someone is allergic to nuts or planned a surprise.
quizzes.payoff: Found-clue score with a revealed list of hotspots and why each mattered.
quizzes.audience: Visual puzzle fans and family groups
quizzes.production_note: Needs a hotspot controller and original illustrations with alt text. Commission or create art; accessibility review is required.

quizzes.title: Group Photo Staging Puzzle
quizzes.hook: Arrange fictional friends for a group photo using height, light and pose clues.
rounds: 3 grids: place people in the frame by clues
3 checks: choose the fix for a flawed layout
quizzes.seed: Dana stands left of the tall tree, Omar holds the banner centered, and the youngest needs the front row. Place all four.
quizzes.payoff: Layout score with partial credit and a gallery of the correct arrangements, explained.
quizzes.audience: Visual puzzle fans and event organizers
quizzes.production_note: Needs a drag-and-place visual component and original character art. Accessibility alternative required; test solvability.

quizzes.title: Pass the Prompt Postcard
quizzes.hook: Send a shared prompt to friends, let everyone answer in their own time, then reveal the postcard together.
rounds: 4 prompts: choose your answer
2 prompts: predict the group's top pick
1 reveal: unlock the postcard
quizzes.seed: Postcard prompt: if our group had a theme song for Friday, would it be upbeat, dreamy or dramatic?
quizzes.payoff: Group postcard with everyone's picks side by side and a playful label like Mixed Mood Crew.
quizzes.audience: Friend groups spread across schedules or places
quizzes.production_note: Needs asynchronous invites, consent, and private-by-default sharing with easy delete. Moderate shared text; no real-name requirements. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Guess the Opt-In Crowd
quizzes.hook: Predict which light party-choice options real, consenting respondents picked most often.
rounds: 6 prompts: guess the most common option
3 prompts: order options as the survey did
quizzes.seed: For movie night, which snack did respondents choose most: popcorn, fruit or candy? Prompt only; no answer exists yet.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score with each real result explained and sample size shown; never an estimated percentile.
quizzes.audience: Party hosts and trivia-style groups
quizzes.production_note: HOLD until a real opt-in survey sample exists. Never use placeholder or fabricated responses. Publish sample size, dates and method note.

quizzes.title: Invitation Relay
quizzes.hook: Pass a fictional invitation around: each person adds one useful detail, and the next removes a contradiction.
rounds: 4 draft cards: choose a sentence meeting the stated event constraints
3 relay edits: remove a contradictory detail
1 final ordering: assemble the group invitation
quizzes.seed: The fictional event is indoors and starts at six. Which added sentence conflicts: bring a board game, arrive at six, or meet on the roof?
quizzes.payoff: A completed invitation card, plus conflicts caught out of seven; cooperative score with explanations.
quizzes.audience: Event organizers and student club leaders
quizzes.production_note: Single-device turns; original fictional venues and fixed constraints. Keep every factual contradiction explicit; no private addresses or contact details.

quizzes.title: Split It Squad
quizzes.hook: Work out a shared bill for a fictional outing, then pick which fairness approach your group prefers.
rounds: 4 bills: calculate each share
4 pairs: choose a splitting approach
2 shared costs: order who covers what
quizzes.seed: Four friends share a $48 tab; one skipped dessert ($8). Split evenly, or each pays for their own items?
quizzes.payoff: Two cards: math score with explanations, and a playful Even Split vs Itemized Split style.
quizzes.audience: Roommates, travelers and friend groups
quizzes.production_note: Knowledge and preference results shown separately. Author and double-check all math. Use currency-neutral amounts; avoid money-status assumptions. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Store and display knowledge accuracy separately from preference results.

quizzes.title: Party Role Draft
quizzes.hook: Draft roles for a fictional event, then see how your picks complement the rest of the group.
rounds: 5 draft picks: choose a role in turn
3 swaps: trade a role for a different task
quizzes.seed: Pick three of: playlist wrangler, snack scout, game referee, greeter, cleanup captain. Then trade one away.
quizzes.payoff: Role card with your picks and a playful pair like Setup Spark vs Wrap-Up Steady.
quizzes.audience: Friend groups and teams planning events
quizzes.production_note: Needs draft-order group scoring. Keep every role valued, with none framed as lesser. Pilot by passing one device. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Requires separate participant state and controlled reveals even when passing one device; add preference aggregation only where explicitly defined.

quizzes.title: Icebreaker Ladder
quizzes.hook: Climb light-to-deeper prompts and let each person choose how far to go, skipping freely.
rounds: 4 light prompts: pick one answer or skip
3 medium prompts: pick or swap prompt
2 warm prompts: choose a response
quizzes.seed: Level 1: Would you rather start a meeting with a joke, a playlist or a one-word check-in?
quizzes.payoff: Ladder card showing the level your group chose together, labeled Lighthearted to Reflective. No pressure ranking.
quizzes.audience: New groups, clubs and workshops
quizzes.production_note: Needs skip-friendly scoring. Prompts reviewed for sensitivity and trauma-awareness; no relationship judgments. Consent screen before play. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Requires separate participant state and controlled reveals even when passing one device; add preference aggregation only where explicitly defined.

quizzes.title: Everyone Gets Something Swap
quizzes.hook: Trade items among fictional friends so each person ends up with what they wanted.
rounds: 3 offer maps: connect each offered item to the person who wants it
3 exchange checks: select the simultaneous swap satisfying every stated need
quizzes.seed: Ana offers a scarf and wants a book; Ben offers a book and wants gloves; Cy offers gloves and wants a scarf. Find the simultaneous exchange.
quizzes.payoff: Six completed exchanges with each closed cycle explained.
quizzes.audience: Logic fans and group-puzzle players
quizzes.production_note: Uses one-to-one match and order controls. Author grids with unique solutions and playtest before release. Use simultaneous exchanges, not an impossible pairwise trade order. Every item needs a stated owner and recipient.

quizzes.title: The Lost-and-Found Relay
quizzes.hook: Work through an invented library's lost-and-found log: match objects to owners, trace desks and time slots, and plan the pickups.
rounds: 1 match and 1 choice: pair objects with owners and desks from clues
2 link maps and 1 grid: draw every desk and slot rule that applies, decoys included
1 ordering and 2 choices: plan the release order and the pickup slots
quizzes.seed: Dev's item opens a door; the Front Desk releases anything valuable or paper. Which item does Dev collect, and where?
quizzes.payoff: Eight checked answers, each with the rule that decides it.
quizzes.audience: Friends, families and clubs who like a shared clue puzzle; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Self-contained original data; every task restates all rules and node labels it needs. Each answer is uniquely determined by the stated rules. No pass-and-play or network features claimed. Distinct from the gift, carpool and invitation puzzles. Library context only, no endorsement implied.

quizzes.title: Continuity Detective
quizzes.hook: Spot the mismatched detail in original written scene notes and learn how crews keep a shoot consistent.
rounds: 4 scene notes: choose the detail that breaks continuity
3 cases: pick which crew role should have caught it
3 shoot-day lists: order takes so the scene stays consistent
quizzes.seed: Scene note: Mia pours coffee into a full mug, then later lifts it empty without drinking. Which detail breaks continuity?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 10 with a short explanation of each continuity trap.
quizzes.audience: Film fans and curious casual viewers, all ages
quizzes.production_note: All scenes are original fictional notes. Source crew-role definitions from published industry references and have a working film professional review answers.

quizzes.title: Your Rewatch Ritual Style
quizzes.hook: Discover whether your comfort-watch habits lean toward familiar favorites or fresh discoveries, and whether you watch solo or with others.
rounds: 6 pairs: choose focused detail-hunting or comforting background viewing
3 scenarios: choose isolated scenes or a complete rewatch
quizzes.seed: Which sounds more like you: rewatching one favorite scene three times, or starting a random unseen title tonight?
quizzes.payoff: Rewatch card: Background Comfort vs Detail-Hunting and Scene-Hopping vs Full-Story Replay.
quizzes.audience: Casual viewers in US, Canada, Mexico; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Original habit wording only, no title dependencies. Review for neutral tone toward theaters, TV, and streaming. Spanish and French need human adaptation. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Author balanced items specifically for these named dimensions; do not reuse generic Plan/Improvise or Solo/Shared vectors.

quizzes.title: Film Craft Decoder
quizzes.hook: Identify what filmmakers did with cameras, edits and lighting using original scene descriptions.
rounds: 4 terms: match techniques to sourced plain-language definitions
4 scene descriptions: identify the stated camera or editing action
3 contrasts: distinguish similar techniques using explicitly described actions
quizzes.seed: A sequence alternates between two simultaneous scenes. Which supplied editing term describes that structure?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a craft glossary card for missed terms.
quizzes.audience: Aspiring filmmakers and fans curious about technique
quizzes.production_note: Source technical definitions and regional terminology. Use original text scenes, no clips. Score observable technique descriptions, not assumed emotional effects or directors’ intentions.

quizzes.title: Adaptation Switchboard
quizzes.hook: Solve original adaptation briefs by connecting proposed edits to explicit production constraints.
rounds: 5 brief constraints: connect proposed edits to the stated requirement each satisfies
5 connected edits: identify compatible combinations, with repeated constraint targets allowed
quizzes.seed: A brief permits one location and ten minutes. Link each proposed edit to the explicit constraint it satisfies.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score with a map showing which connections were one-to-one and which were shared.
quizzes.audience: Readers, gamers, and viewers who compare source and screen
quizzes.production_note: Use original fictional briefs with explicit production constraints, not guesses about real creators’ intentions. Declare all valid links and normalize graph credit.

quizzes.title: Cozy or Creepy Scene Lab
quizzes.hook: Learn which light, sound, and pacing ingredients make a scene feel cozy or creepy, then see which you prefer.
rounds: 4 original scenes: choose which atmosphere you personally prefer
4 craft terms: match defined techniques to supplied examples
quizzes.seed: Warm lamp, soft rain, slow pacing versus empty hallway, humming lights, long silence: which recipe would you rather linger in?
quizzes.payoff: Four craft answers plus a separate atmosphere preference card; cozy/creepy choices have no correct answer.
quizzes.audience: Seasonal mood-seekers and cinema fans, US and Canada
quizzes.production_note: Needs separate knowledge and preference scoring. Recipes are original text and genre-neutral. Canadian whimsy and liminal trends are interest signals only; no clip use. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Store and display knowledge accuracy separately from preference results.

quizzes.title: The Unreliable Narrator Files
quizzes.hook: Read original case files told by shaky narrators and work out which claims the evidence actually supports.
rounds: 3 fictional case files: pick the claim contradicted by the supplied reliable evidence
2 case files: order events using explicit timestamp clues
quizzes.seed: The reliable entry log records a 9:10 departure. The narrator claims she stayed inside from nine to ten. Which claim conflicts?
quizzes.payoff: Grid score out of 5 with a note on how each narrator's story cracked.
quizzes.audience: Mystery and twist-film fans, teens to adults
quizzes.production_note: All narrations are original fictional files with unique solutions. Playtest each for a single defensible answer; avoid referencing real twist endings or spoilers.

quizzes.title: Cinema Across Three Borders
quizzes.hook: Test what you know about film and TV traditions from the US, Canada, and Mexico, including shared productions.
rounds: 4 US prompts: match works to context
4 Canada prompts: group works by production origin
4 Mexico prompts: match works to context
quizzes.seed: Group these titles by production country; some may belong to more than one country because of co-production.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score per country plus a combined total with source-backed explanations.
quizzes.audience: North American film fans; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Gate: cultural reviewers from each country check titles, credits, and co-production status. French and Spanish editions need human adaptation, not translation. Avoid canon bias.

quizzes.title: A Movie in Three Timelines
quizzes.hook: Order one film's story chronology, its making, and its release history to see how three timelines differ.
rounds: 4 story events: order by in-story chronology
4 making milestones: order by production stage
3 release steps: order by public rollout
quizzes.seed: A named film’s supplied source cards date its script draft, principal photography and release. Arrange those documented milestones on three parallel timelines.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a three-lane timeline summary.
quizzes.audience: Fans who like film history and behind-the-scenes trivia
quizzes.production_note: Choose films with fully documented chronologies; verify every date with primary sources. Recent titles are edition candidates pending official source recheck. Use dated records for one specific film, not a universal production order; revisions and announcements can overlap filming.

quizzes.title: Animation Technique Lab
quizzes.hook: Figure out how hand-drawn, stop-motion, and computer animation get made, using original diagrams.
rounds: 4 diagrams: identify which technique each shows
4 step lists: order a technique's workflow
3 effects: choose the method that creates it
quizzes.seed: A clay figure moved slightly between photographed frames: which technique is this, and what limits its speed?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a technique cheat-sheet card.
quizzes.audience: Animation fans and families with older kids
quizzes.production_note: Needs original generic diagrams drawn for this quiz; no studio stills or frames. Technique descriptions sourced from published animation references. Alt text required.

quizzes.title: Writers' Room Relay
quizzes.hook: Build a silly original logline with friends by each adding one story ingredient, then rate the combo.
rounds: 3 rounds: each player picks a genre, hook, or twist card
2 rounds: group votes on which pitch to polish
quizzes.seed: Player one picks 'heist-free road trip', player two adds 'a haunted vending machine'. What twist closes the pitch?
quizzes.payoff: A shareable group logline card and a mix of genre cards chosen.
quizzes.audience: Friend groups, families, and watch-party hosts
quizzes.production_note: Needs asynchronous or host-based group sessions. Card pool is original and content-reviewed; no real-person or title references. Moderation for free-text if added.

quizzes.title: Trailer Grammar
quizzes.hook: Recognize the editing moves trailers use to build hype, from quiet openings to the big title drop.
rounds: 5 described trailers: name the technique being used
4 beats: order a classic trailer structure
quizzes.seed: A trailer goes silent, shows one line of dialogue, then slams to a title card. Which technique is this?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 9 with a quick trailer-structure explainer.
quizzes.audience: Casual moviegoers curious about marketing craft
quizzes.production_note: Trailers are described with original fictional examples; no real trailer footage or audio. Technique names sourced from published marketing or editing references.

quizzes.title: Read the Rating Label
quizzes.hook: Decode what official screen-rating labels and content advisories actually tell you across named jurisdictions.
rounds: 4 labels: connect a named ratings authority to its published category definition
4 advisories: match the official wording to its stated content meaning
4 comparisons: identify what cannot be concluded from a label alone
quizzes.seed: A label supplies an age category and a violence advisory. Which describes stated content, and which describes the age classification?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score per system with a comparison note, not a verdict on which is stricter.
quizzes.audience: Parents, students, and curious moviegoers in North America
quizzes.production_note: Verify official definitions by authority, jurisdiction and date; Canada has multiple systems. Never predict ratings for invented scenes or imply suitability advice.

quizzes.title: One Actor, Three Worlds
quizzes.hook: Connect very different screen roles that turn out to share one credited performer, including voice performances.
rounds: 4 role cards: connect roles to credited performers, with repeated performer targets
4 film cards: link those performances to release decades
3 crossover reveals: identify the missing role in a performer’s verified chain
quizzes.seed: Connect Neo in The Matrix (1999), John Wick in John Wick (2014), and Duke Caboom in Toy Story 4 (2019) to credited performer and release decade.
quizzes.payoff: A performer-role-decade web with edge accuracy and a surprising credited connection.
quizzes.audience: Credit-stayers and aspiring crew members
quizzes.production_note: Verify every role and release against official film credits and studio records. Original text cards only; distinguish voice, cameo and credited character names.

quizzes.title: TV Episode Anatomy
quizzes.hook: Learn the parts of a TV episode, from cold opens to A, B, and C stories.
rounds: 4 terms: match each TV structure term to its meaning
4 original outlines: order episode beats
3 outlines: identify the format being used
quizzes.seed: An episode set in one room with a small cast: which format term describes it best?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a glossary of episode formats.
quizzes.audience: TV fans and aspiring writers
quizzes.production_note: Outlines are original; terms sourced from writing-craft references. Avoid claiming one structure is universal across all networks, streamers, and countries.

quizzes.title: Season Shape Preference
quizzes.hook: Find your taste for short tight seasons versus long sprawling ones, and for weekly versus binge release.
rounds: 6 pair choices: pick the season shape you would rather watch
3 scenarios: choose how you would spend a watch-night
quizzes.seed: Would you rather watch eight tight episodes in one weekend or twenty loose ones across a season?
quizzes.payoff: Playful summary on pace-versus-sprawl and weekly-versus-binge; not a fixed identity.
quizzes.audience: Streaming and TV viewers; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs new two-axis preference scoring. Options use no real titles. Review for neutrality toward platforms and no claim that either preference is better. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Sound Design Ear Test
quizzes.hook: Listen to original sound effects and guess what made them and the mood they build.
rounds: 5 clips: identify the everyday sound source
4 clips: choose the mood or effect each sound suggests
quizzes.seed: Original clip: crunching sounds with a slow rhythm. Is this snow, gravel, or cereal, and what mood does it add?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 9 with a short note on how foley works.
quizzes.audience: Sound-curious fans, headphone users
quizzes.production_note: All audio recorded or composed originally; no film clips. Captions and text alternatives required for accessibility. Mood answers are interpretive and need careful reviewer wording. Key only explicit stated requirements or intended effects in the supplied brief; interpretive taste judgments remain unscored and may have multiple valid answers.

quizzes.title: Fan Theory Evidence Board
quizzes.hook: Test a fictional fan theory by sorting clues into supports, weakens, or neutral.
rounds: 4 evidence boards: sort each clue by how it affects the theory
2 boards: choose the strongest and weakest clue
quizzes.seed: Theory: the butler planted the key. Clue: the key was found before he arrived. Supports, weakens, or neutral?
quizzes.payoff: Grid score out of 6 with an explanation of how each clue changes the theory.
quizzes.audience: Puzzle-minded fans of mystery TV and film
quizzes.production_note: Fully original fictional show and theories; no real fandoms. Each board needs one defensible key; playtest ambiguity and avoid trick wording.

quizzes.title: Wardrobe Story Reader
quizzes.hook: Read what costume and set choices say about a character's arc in original written examples.
rounds: 4 costume notes: choose the story point they signal
4 set notes: match the design choice to its purpose
quizzes.seed: A character's coat shrinks to dull gray after a loss. What story purpose might that costume change serve?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 8 with a design-language explainer.
quizzes.audience: Costume, design, and character-study enthusiasts
quizzes.production_note: Examples are original fictional notes. Answers are interpretive, so authors source design principles and avoid single-meaning color claims across cultures. Key only explicit stated requirements or intended effects in the supplied brief; interpretive taste judgments remain unscored and may have multiple valid answers.

quizzes.title: Movie Tech Problem Solvers
quizzes.hook: Match technologies that changed filmmaking to the problems they solved, from sound to digital effects.
rounds: 5 technologies: match each to the problem it solved
4 milestones: order them from earliest to latest
quizzes.seed: Match 'synchronized sound' and 'digital projection' to the filmmaking or exhibition problem each addressed.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 9 with a mini-timeline of tech eras.
quizzes.audience: Film history fans and tech-curious viewers
quizzes.production_note: Every date and attribution verified against published film-history sources. Avoid sole-inventor claims. Reviewer checks that US-centric framing is balanced with other regions.

quizzes.title: Showrunner's Season Planner
quizzes.hook: Make planning choices for an imaginary show season and see your creative style.
rounds: 4 planning branches: choose a story direction each step
3 final picks: choose an ending style and release plan
quizzes.seed: Your pilot lands well: do you expand the cast, deepen the lead's mystery, or try a standalone episode?
quizzes.payoff: Playful style summary on risk-versus-consistency and character-versus-plot; not a skill ranking.
quizzes.audience: Creative viewers and aspiring writers
quizzes.production_note: Needs a new branching journey and result mapping. Fictional show only; choices are original. Playtest that no path reads as the 'correct' creative style. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Three Ways to Follow the Dialogue
quizzes.hook: Untangle captions, subtitles and dubbing, then choose which screen-access feature solves a stated viewing need.
rounds: 4 scenarios: select the feature meeting the explicitly stated need
4 matches: connect terminology to examples using original dialogue
quizzes.seed: A fictional viewer wants written dialogue plus relevant sound cues in the same language. Which listed feature provides both?
quizzes.payoff: Accuracy out of eight with explanations of access features and regional terminology.
quizzes.audience: Viewers curious about habits; US, Canada, Mexico
quizzes.production_note: Verify terminology with accessibility and media-standard sources; acknowledge overlapping usage. Use original example dialogue, never copied subtitles.

quizzes.title: How Scares Work
quizzes.hook: Sort scenes by the mechanic that frightens, from slow dread to the sudden jump, using original examples.
rounds: 4 scenes: name the scare mechanic
4 mechanics: match each to the effect it creates
3 building steps: order how a tense scene builds
quizzes.seed: A long quiet hallway shot where nothing happens yet. Is this dread, a jump scare, or an uncanny moment?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a glossary of scare techniques.
quizzes.audience: Seasonal horror fans, non-gory, teens to adults
quizzes.production_note: Scenes are original and non-graphic. Mechanic terms sourced from published horror-craft writing. Seasonal search interest is only a timing signal, not quiz demand.

quizzes.title: Documentary, Docudrama, or Mockumentary?
quizzes.hook: Tell nonfiction and fake-nonfiction film forms apart with original described examples.
rounds: 5 descriptions: classify each as a documentary form
4 features: choose the form each is signalling
quizzes.seed: A fictional comedy filmed with talking-head interviews and shaky handheld camera: which form fits?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 9 with an explainer for each form.
quizzes.audience: Film students and documentary curious viewers
quizzes.production_note: Examples are original and fictional. Definitions sourced from published documentary studies; reviewer checks boundary cases so answers have a defensible single key.

quizzes.title: Story Shapes: Telenovela to Anthology
quizzes.hook: Match TV series formats to the kind of storytelling promise each makes, across traditions.
rounds: 5 formats: match each to its storytelling promise
4 original series pitches: identify the format
quizzes.seed: A series with a self-contained story each episode and a new cast every season: which format fits?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 9 with a format glossary and examples.
quizzes.audience: TV fans across North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Gate: Mexican telenovela conventions and other regional forms reviewed by culturally informed editors. Pitches are original; no real title examples unless verified.

quizzes.title: Poster Grammar Lab
quizzes.hook: Decode the layout, color, and text conventions of movie posters using original mock-up diagrams.
rounds: 4 mock-ups: identify the poster convention shown
4 genre mock-ups: choose the genre the design signals
3 layout lists: order elements by visual hierarchy
quizzes.seed: A mock poster with a tiny figure under a huge dark sky: what mood or genre does that layout usually suggest?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 11 with a visual-convention cheat-sheet.
quizzes.audience: Design-minded movie fans, all ages
quizzes.production_note: All posters are original generic mock-ups; no real posters, logos, or stills. Genre signals are conventions, not rules, and need design-reference sourcing and alt text. Key only explicit stated requirements or intended effects in the supplied brief; interpretive taste judgments remain unscored and may have multiple valid answers.

quizzes.title: Build the Opening Three Songs
quizzes.hook: Design the first three moments of a set using mood cards instead of song titles, then see your opening style.
rounds: 3 openers: order described moods into a set
4 pairs: choose the stronger first-song promise
quizzes.seed: Your room is half-full and nervous. Which opener fits: a slow-building groove, a loud shared chorus, or a quiet spotlight moment?

quizzes.hook: Help friends in different cities agree on a fair meeting place using distance reasoning.
rounds: 4 group scenarios: choose a fair meeting region
3 pairs: compare travel burdens together
quizzes.seed: Three fictional friends have the displayed travel times to four venues. Which venue minimizes the longest journey, then which compromise does everyone prefer?
quizzes.payoff: Group agreement summary showing shared picks and where views differed; no ranking of players.
quizzes.audience: Friend groups and families spread across cities
quizzes.production_note: Needs asynchronous group sessions and privacy review. Use approximate distances only; no cost or safety advice. Fictional cities allowed. Show fixed travel times; separate the objective minimax answer from subjective fairness preference.

quizzes.title: Detour Diary: Prairie to Pacific
quizzes.hook: Make route decisions on a fictional cross-Canada trip and see how geography shapes each outcome.
rounds: 6 branching choices: pick your next move
3 recap questions: explain why it worked
quizzes.seed: Fog closes the mountain pass at Fern Gap. Do you wait, take the longer inland highway, or reroute to the ferry?
quizzes.payoff: Journey summary with the geographic reason behind each branch; no scoring against real routes.
quizzes.audience: Story-driven puzzle fans and road-trip dreamers
quizzes.production_note: Use fictional places so conditions never go stale; needs a branching journey format and playtests. No real safety or road advice.

quizzes.title: Names Layered on North America's Map
quizzes.hook: Discover how Indigenous, French, Spanish, and English place names stack up across the continent.
rounds: 4 names: match each to a language layer
4 names: sort into origin groups (many-to-one)
3 archive snippets: choose which spelling or naming claim the cited record supports
quizzes.seed: Match e.g. Saskatchewan, Montréal, and Los Angeles to the language layer their names come from.
quizzes.payoff: Score by layer with each name's origin explained; no claims beyond sourced etymology.
quizzes.audience: Language and history-minded players across Canada, Mexico, and the US
quizzes.production_note: Gate: Indigenous language and community review for every etymology; no folk etymologies. French and Spanish editions need human adaptation. Include current Indigenous usage where relevant; language origins can be disputed or layered, so accept documented alternatives and never ask for a dominant culture.

quizzes.title: Seen From Orbit: Why It Looks That Way
quizzes.hook: Look at satellite-style patterns and work out what caused them.
rounds: 4 images: choose the cause
4 images: match pattern to land use
quizzes.seed: An image shows neat green circles in dry land. Is the likeliest cause center-pivot irrigation, volcanic vents, or meteor craters?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 with each pattern explained in text; no percentile.
quizzes.audience: Visual learners and geography fans
quizzes.production_note: Use properly licensed or original imagery with full alt text. Verify each pattern with sources; every question must work from a text description.

quizzes.title: Read the Climate Chart
quizzes.hook: Match temperature and rainfall charts to the kinds of places that produce them.
rounds: 4 charts: choose the climate type
4 charts: match to a region type
quizzes.seed: A chart shows a wet winter and a dry summer. Which fits better: Pacific coast, central plains, or tropical lowlands?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 with a plain-text description of each chart's shape.
quizzes.audience: Students and curious travelers
quizzes.production_note: Charts need source-checked data and a data-table alternative for every chart. Avoid current weather or forecast claims.

quizzes.title: Hear the Landscape
quizzes.hook: Listen to a simple terrain profile encoded as original tones, then connect what you hear to a map.
rounds: 4 original tone sequences: match pitch changes to a supplied elevation profile
4 route choices: select the path consistent with the explicit sound-to-elevation legend
quizzes.seed: Higher pitch means higher ground. A tone rises, stays level, then drops. Which of the three described route profiles fits?
quizzes.payoff: Eight terrain connections with explanations and a text version of each sound sequence.
quizzes.audience: Players who enjoy sensory puzzles
quizzes.production_note: Commission original non-musical tones with a fixed legend. Provide equivalent numeric or verbal profiles; score legend use, not hearing acuity.

quizzes.title: Passenger Seat Rules
quizzes.hook: Pick your road-trip rules, then see how your choices compare once enough players opt in.
rounds: 6 pairs: choose your passenger-seat preferences
3 rankings: prioritize your own stopping, navigation and conversation choices
quizzes.seed: On a long drive, would you rather stop at every viewpoint or keep going until dinner?
quizzes.payoff: Passenger card: Scenic Stops vs Steady Mileage and Navigation Duties vs Atmosphere Duties.
quizzes.audience: Road-trip groups and families
quizzes.production_note: No public polling or fabricated crowd comparison. Keep choices private by default; offer an optional user-controlled share card. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Author balanced items specifically for these named dimensions; do not reuse generic Plan/Improvise or Solo/Shared vectors.

quizzes.title: Itinerary Sanity Check
quizzes.hook: Repair a fictional day plan by finding backtracking and clock clashes in its supplied travel-time table.
rounds: 3 sample plans: spot the clash
3 plans: order stops to reduce backtracking
quizzes.seed: Plan: breakfast in the north, lunch in the south, park gate at the north, dinner in the south. What would you reorder?
quizzes.payoff: Six route-repair decisions with clear time and ordering explanations; no personal itinerary submission.
quizzes.audience: Players who like fixing plans
quizzes.production_note: All plans are fictional with fixed travel-time tables. Deterministic constraints and explanations; no AI or current travel advice required.

quizzes.title: Flat Map, Round World
quizzes.hook: Discover how flat maps change what looks large, near or straight, then solve a route puzzle on a globe.
rounds: 4 projection diagrams: identify the property distorted under the supplied legend
4 globe-route comparisons: select the shorter great-circle path using provided measurements
quizzes.seed: Two maps use different projections. Use the equal-area legend to decide which drawing supports an area comparison.
quizzes.payoff: Eight map-reading decisions with projection and route explanations.
quizzes.audience: Pairs, friends, and classrooms
quizzes.production_note: Use original verified cartographic diagrams and text equivalents. Geometric distance is not a claim about real airline routes or travel advice.

quizzes.title: Backyard Evidence Lab
quizzes.hook: Treat a patch of ordinary ground like a case file and decide which clues actually support which explanation.
rounds: 4 clue sets: choose the best-supported explanation
4 field notes: order observe, question, test
3 pairs: match clue to likely cause
quizzes.seed: In a labeled fictional observation table, sheltered boxes have more woodlice across repeated counts. Which conclusion is supported, and which would require an experiment?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus a one-line reason for each miss; no percentile.
quizzes.audience: Curious teens and adults; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Source every answer from museum, university extension or research-institution field guides; review for region-neutral wording, no handling of wildlife, and no unsafe outdoor tasks. Use clearly labeled synthetic observation tables or cited real datasets; distinguish correlation from cause.

quizzes.title: Moon Mission Control
quizzes.hook: Make the calls mission planners face, from launch to splashdown, and see why each step comes before the next.
rounds: 3 launch calls: order the steps
3 transit problems: pick the best response
3 return puzzles: match constraint to reason
quizzes.seed: Why might a mission plan a path that loops the Moon and heads home, rather than orbiting first? Pick the best reason.
quizzes.payoff: Mission log score with a short explanation of each decision; flags that this is a simplified model.
quizzes.audience: Space-curious teens and adults; US/Canada focus; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Author only from NASA/CSA public materials, cite each answer internally, avoid claims about real crew events beyond sources; expert review for orbital simplifications.

quizzes.title: Scale Shock
quizzes.hook: Put surprising things in size order and find out which of your instincts about big and small hold up.
rounds: 5 sets: order four items smallest to largest
4 pairs: choose which is larger and by roughly how much
quizzes.seed: Order the four labeled specimens by their supplied measured diameters; then compare them with a scale bar.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus a scale ladder showing every item in its true order.
quizzes.audience: Anyone who likes surprising comparisons; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Verify each size against a museum or research-institution reference with explicit units and ranges; avoid comparisons where definitions vary. Give concrete specimen measurements; broad ranges for hair, sand and cells can overlap.

quizzes.title: Weather Without the Forecast
quizzes.hook: Read the sky, wind and air clues yourself and predict what is coming before any app tells you.
rounds: 3 sky clues: choose the likeliest change
3 chains: order clue, cause, outcome
3 scenarios: pick what to watch next
quizzes.seed: Given the displayed pressure trend, cloud sequence and model assumptions, which of the listed changes best fits the evidence?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus a clue-to-outcome chain for each answer; not a forecast tool.
quizzes.audience: Hikers, gardeners, weather fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Source from NOAA or national weather service education material; regional review (Canada, US, Mexico); never present quiz output as safety guidance. Include uncertainty and all required evidence; no real-weather forecast or safety guidance.

quizzes.title: Mystery Material
quizzes.hook: Work out why a material suits a job by matching the needs of an object to the properties that explain them.
rounds: 4 grids: match each need to a property
2 grids: match object to best material
quizzes.seed: A kettle handle must stay cool, resist cracking and mold easily. Match each need to the property that explains it.
quizzes.payoff: Grids solved with a property-reasoning summary; no physics-superiority claims.
quizzes.audience: Makers, students, tinkerers; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Source property statements from engineering or museum materials references; avoid trade-name claims, and use reasoning only, with no experiments requiring heat or chemicals.

quizzes.title: Build a Food Web
quizzes.hook: Wire up who eats whom in a habitat, then predict how a missing species ripples through it.
rounds: 3 habitat grids: link species to food sources, many-to-one
3 disruption grids: predict first and second effects
quizzes.seed: The supplied food web shows fish eating grazers and birds eating fish. Remove fish: which direct feeding links disappear?
quizzes.payoff: Web completed, links correct, plus a ripple diagram of the three effect layers.
quizzes.audience: Nature fans and students; North America habitats; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Each habitat needs ecologist review of links and ripple claims; use partial credit; limit to well-documented relationships. Show a simplified explicit web; distinguish direct link loss from uncertain ecosystem-wide population predictions.

quizzes.title: Where Was the Light?
quizzes.hook: Read the direction and length of shadows to work out where the light is and what time it could be.
rounds: 4 controlled shadow diagrams: select the light direction using stated geometry
2 controlled diagrams: choose the change in light elevation matching the shadow-length change
quizzes.seed: Two equal-height posts stand on level ground under one distant light. Use the supplied compass directions to locate the light from their shadows.
quizzes.payoff: Scenes cracked with a light-angle explanation; no deterministic ranking.
quizzes.audience: Visual thinkers, photographers, teens; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs original illustrated or rendered scenes with alt text and a text-only fallback; verify geometry with a science reviewer. No time-of-day inference without date, latitude and orientation; these rounds test explicitly supplied geometry.

quizzes.title: The Sound You Cannot See
quizzes.hook: Listen to a short clip and work out what the sound traveled through and why it changed.
rounds: 4 clips: choose the medium or source
3 clip pairs: pick which changed and why
quizzes.seed: A thump sounds muffled behind a wall and sharp in open air. Which change in the path explains it?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus what each clip revealed; not a hearing test.
quizzes.audience: Audio and science fans; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs original recordings with transcripts and captions, a no-audio text route, and an explicit statement that this is not a hearing assessment.

quizzes.title: The Pollinator Shift
quizzes.hook: Guide a garden through three seasons and see how timing between plants and pollinators shapes what happens.
rounds: 3 spring scenarios: choose a planting response
3 summer scenarios: choose a response
3 autumn scenarios: choose a response
quizzes.seed: Early flowers fade before bees emerge. Which helps a timing gap: stagger bloom times, add one flower type, or neither?
quizzes.payoff: Knowledge score plus a playful garden-style summary on two dimensions: patience and variety.
quizzes.audience: Gardeners, nature-journal fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs entomologist or extension-service review; keep knowledge and preference results separate; regional plant examples checked per country. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Store and display knowledge accuracy separately from preference results.

quizzes.title: Cause Chain Courtroom
quizzes.hook: Judge a three-step cause chain and find the link where the argument is weakest.
rounds: 4 grids: match each link to its supporting mechanism
2 grids: find the broken link, many-to-one allowed
quizzes.seed: More leaf litter, then more decomposers feeding, then what change in soil nutrients? Which link needs the strongest evidence?
quizzes.payoff: Chains judged, with a weakest-link note on each; no fabricated percentiles.
quizzes.audience: Debaters, students, careful thinkers; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use only chains with sourced mechanisms; each link validated independently to avoid compounding errors; reviewer must confirm no step is oversimplified.

quizzes.title: Field Notebook Style
quizzes.hook: Choose between pairs of observation moments to see how you tend to notice nature.
rounds: 6 observation scenarios: choose what you would record first
2 short rankings: prioritize detail, pattern and change in a field note
quizzes.seed: On a woodland path you can record one thing first: a leaf's texture or the pattern of birdsong. Which?
quizzes.payoff: Playful notebook style on two axes: details vs patterns, sketching vs counting; not an identity.
quizzes.audience: Nature-journalers and hobbyists; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs new pair-preference scoring and a copy review stating no style is better; no psychometric claims. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Tiny Terrarium Logic
quizzes.hook: Plan a sealed miniature habitat on paper and predict what each change does to its small cycles.
rounds: 3 build grids: match component to role, many-to-one
3 change grids: predict three-step effects
quizzes.seed: In the supplied model, reducing light lowers plant growth. Which link changes directly, and which downstream effect is not specified?
quizzes.payoff: Jar balanced with partial credit and a cycle diagram; digital only, no home experiment.
quizzes.audience: Miniature and plant hobbyists; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs horticulture or ecology review; explicitly no instructions for building or handling materials; avoid claims about closed-jar longevity. Provide model assumptions; do not infer real terrarium moisture or soil-life changes from light alone.

quizzes.title: Where Did the Energy Go
quizzes.hook: Trace energy through everyday events like a swinging pendulum or a campfire and find where it ends up.
rounds: 4 sequences: order the energy transfers
4 scenarios: choose where the energy went
quizzes.seed: A rolling ball slows to a stop. Where does its motion energy go: choose the best account.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus an energy flow summary for each scenario.
quizzes.audience: Teens and adults; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Physics reviewer must check wording on energy conservation and avoid any link to the existing physics interest assessment.

quizzes.title: Fair Test Designer
quizzes.hook: Pick what to change, keep and measure so a simple plant or ramp test gives a trustworthy answer.
rounds: 4 designs: choose what must stay the same
2 designs: find the flaw
quizzes.seed: Two seedlings sit in different pots and one gets more light. What must stay the same for a fair comparison?
quizzes.payoff: Designs graded with a short fair-test checklist.
quizzes.audience: Students, parents, teachers; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use only conceptual designs; no hazardous materials; science educator review of wording and curriculum fit.

quizzes.title: Rock Cycle Road Trip
quizzes.hook: Follow one rock as it faces heat, weather and pressure, choosing what happens to it at each fork.
rounds: 3 rock-cycle forks: select the change supported by stated temperature and pressure
3 consequence forks: trace the resulting material using a supplied reference diagram
quizzes.seed: A rock sits buried under pressure for a very long time. Which change is likeliest next, and why?
quizzes.payoff: Journey map of the rock's path with a reason for each turn.
quizzes.audience: Geology fans and students; North America landscapes; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs a new branching journey; geoscientist review of simplified paths; use geological survey or museum sources.

quizzes.title: Night Sky Clue Hunt
quizzes.hook: Tap clues on a sky image to explain what you would see and why it moves or changes.
rounds: 5 sky scenes: tap the clue that answers the question
2 scenes: choose the best explanation
quizzes.seed: Compare dated sky diagrams against fixed background stars. Which object changes position, and what further information would identify it?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score with each clue revealed on the image.
quizzes.audience: Skywatchers and families; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs original hotspot images with alt text and text fallback; astronomer review; latitude and season assumptions stated clearly. Never identify a star or planet from brightness or one still image alone. Supply dates, orientation and adequate motion evidence.

quizzes.title: Who Passed Through Here?
quizzes.hook: Read tracks, scratches and other signs on a scene to work out who passed by.
rounds: 5 scenes: tap the sign and choose the likely visitor
2 scenes: choose what the sign suggests
quizzes.seed: Tap the clue showing the visitor moved quickly, then choose the likeliest explanation.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score with a field-guide note for each scene.
quizzes.audience: Hikers and nature fans; US/Canada/Mexico regional sets
quizzes.production_note: Needs original illustrations and regional wildlife expert review; no hunting or trapping content; avoid disturbing wildlife; separate regional sets.

quizzes.title: Season Reasoning Gauntlet
quizzes.hook: Test the explanations you grew up with about seasons, daylight and sun angle.
rounds: 6 claims: pick the better explanation
3 pairs: match effect to cause
quizzes.seed: Why is summer warmer: Earth is closer to the Sun, or tilt changes daylight and sun angle? Choose.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus a short explanation for each claim.
quizzes.audience: Teens and adults; Northern and Southern Hemisphere both explained
quizzes.production_note: Source from NASA or university astronomy education; check hemisphere-neutral wording; avoid shaming common misconceptions.

quizzes.title: Follow the Drop
quizzes.hook: Trace one raindrop from a mountain to the sea and decide which path it takes at each stage.
rounds: 3 upland choices: order the route
3 river choices: order the route
3 coast choices: match place to process
quizzes.seed: A raindrop lands on snow-covered ground. Order three likely steps before it reaches a stream.
quizzes.payoff: Route map with a process label for each stage.
quizzes.audience: Outdoor fans and students; North America watersheds; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use hydrology sources from NOAA, USGS or Canadian equivalents; avoid claiming a single route; regional review for each watershed example.

quizzes.title: Species Under Pressure
quizzes.hook: Weigh trade-offs in a made-up habitat and see how your choices affect species and your own priorities.
rounds: 6 dilemmas: choose a management action
4 outcomes: match action to likely effect
quizzes.seed: A wetland is drying. Choose between protecting nesting areas now or restoring water flow first, then see the effects.
quizzes.payoff: Knowledge score plus a playful priorities summary on two dimensions; no right-values claim.
quizzes.audience: Conservation-curious adults and teens; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs ecologist review; fictional habitats only; keep knowledge and preference results separate; no political or advocacy claims. Use an explicit fictional ecosystem model; distinguish model-rule outcomes from real conservation recommendations. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Store and display knowledge accuracy separately from preference results.

quizzes.title: Pickles to Pond Osmosis
quizzes.hook: Predict what happens to cells in salty and fresh water using ordinary examples from kitchen and pond.
rounds: 4 scenarios: predict which way water moves
3 pairs: match example to process
quizzes.seed: A slice of cucumber sits in very salty water. Predict what happens to its cells and why.
quizzes.payoff: Raw score plus a water-movement explanation for each scenario.
quizzes.audience: Students and curious cooks; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Biology reviewer checks wording; no health or diagnostic advice; conceptual only with no instructions to experiment.

quizzes.title: Freeze-Thaw Pothole Predictor
quizzes.hook: Follow how water, cold and traffic work together to break up a road and predict what comes next.
rounds: 3 grids: match stage to cause
3 grids: predict three-step damage chains
quizzes.seed: Water seeps into a crack, freezes, then thaws. Which step expands the crack and what follows?
quizzes.payoff: Chains completed with partial credit and a cause diagram.
quizzes.audience: Commuters in cold climates; US/Canada focus; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Source from engineering or transportation research sources; review for simplifications; verify applicability in milder Mexican climates.

quizzes.title: Predict, Reveal, Revise
quizzes.hook: Make a provisional scientific prediction, reveal a new observation, and decide whether the evidence changes your explanation.
rounds: 3 experiments: make an unscored initial prediction from limited evidence
3 reveals: select the conclusion supported by the completed dataset
quizzes.seed: Two explanations fit the first observation. A new labeled experimental result rules one out. Which explanation remains supported?
quizzes.payoff: Three final evidence decisions and a private before/after prediction timeline; no penalty for reasonable initial uncertainty.
quizzes.audience: Friends, families, classrooms; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use clearly labeled synthetic datasets or cited real data. Fixed evidence reveals; score only conclusions supported by the final supplied evidence.

quizzes.title: Spot the Weak Science Claim
quizzes.hook: Read short made-up headlines and find which claim goes further than its evidence supports.
rounds: 4 headlines: choose the overreach
3 headlines: match claim to evidence needed
quizzes.seed: A made-up headline says 'Study proves tea cures sleepiness.' Which part goes beyond a small sample?
quizzes.payoff: Claims judged with a short what-evidence-would-help note.
quizzes.audience: News readers and students; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use invented fictional claims only, never real studies or medical advice; science communicator review of each answer.

quizzes.title: Citizen Science Team Builder
quizzes.hook: Plan a local observation project with friends, dividing roles so the data stays reliable.
rounds: 4 roles: assign the best task
3 data checks: pick which record to trust
quizzes.seed: Your team counts backyard birds weekly. Who should record the time and place, and why does it matter?
quizzes.payoff: Team plan score with a data-quality checklist.
quizzes.audience: Families, clubs, classrooms; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Needs an asynchronous host integration; no real-location sharing, especially for minors; link only to reviewed citizen-science programs. Allocate roles by the activity’s stated requirements and participants’ preferences, never infer abilities from identity.

quizzes.title: Mineral Scratch Lab
quizzes.hook: Learn what scratch-resistance hardness means, then read invented scratch logs to rank mystery samples by the lab's toy rules.
rounds: 4 scale checks: definition, order, matching and what the numbers mean
4 log readings: grid, choices and ordering from invented scratch trials
quizzes.seed: Sample A scratches Sample B, and B scratches C. Is A harder than C, and what would a failed scratch alone tell you?
quizzes.payoff: Scored answers with the scale facts and the log rule behind each one.
quizzes.audience: Curious students and rock-and-mineral fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Scale facts limited to the Mohs order talc 1 to diamond 10 and that it is a relative ordering from USGS Natural Gemstones. Observation tables are original and fictional. No fingernail, coin or glass values, no instructions for real scratch tests, not an identification tool. Toy rules state that a scratch means harder and that no scratch alone does not prove softer.

quizzes.title: Museum of Everyday Objects
quizzes.hook: Read wear, shape and context like a curator to work out what ordinary things were for.
rounds: 4 object cards: choose the most likely use from clues
4 trios: order objects by when they were commonly used
quizzes.seed: A museum record describes a perforated rotating drum that separates flour from coarse bran. Which job fits: sifting, washing, or roasting?
quizzes.payoff: Raw score out of 8, with each answer separating what the object shows from what curators infer.
quizzes.audience: Curious teens and adults; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use objects with documented museum or archival provenance. Source every answer, avoid single-inventor claims, and have a second reviewer check regional variation.

quizzes.title: Before the First iPhone
quizzes.hook: Discover which supposedly smartphone-era habits and technologies were already around before the 2007 iPhone launch.
rounds: 6 scenes: choose before or after from the clues
3 scenes: pick the one detail that breaks the timeline
quizzes.seed: Which already existed before the first iPhone launched in 2007: sending a photo from a camera phone, or this named later app?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 9 plus a timeline strip showing which clue settled each scene.
quizzes.audience: Teens and adults; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use the explicit 2007 product milestone, not a vague smartphone era. Source first availability dates and distinguish invention from mainstream adoption.

quizzes.title: The Archive Has a Missing Page
quizzes.hook: Reconstruct what a lost document must have said, using only the clues in the pages that survive.
rounds: 3 dossiers: order shuffled documents using internal clues
3 gaps: choose what the missing page must say
quizzes.seed: Letter C quotes B’s request for a seed loan. Which missing-page claim is directly established by that quotation?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 6 grids and a case file showing which clues forced each conclusion.
quizzes.audience: Puzzle fans and history students; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Fully fictional archives, so no real person is misrepresented. Playtest that each puzzle has exactly one defensible solution. Require explicit cross-references; narrative plausibility alone cannot make a missing document’s content necessary.

quizzes.title: Fact, Source Claim, or Interpretation?
quizzes.hook: Sort what a record proves from what someone claims or a historian infers, then fix an overreaching label.
rounds: 3 statements: sort as fact, source claim, or interpretation
3 sources: choose what each can and cannot prove
3 labels: pick the wording the evidence supports
quizzes.seed: An unsigned diary claims workers leaving caused the mill closure. Does that excerpt verify causation or only document the diarist’s explanation?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 9 with a note explaining each fact, claim, or interpretation call.
quizzes.audience: Students, teachers and history fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use invented or well-documented cases. Historian reviews every fact versus interpretation split and shows uncertainty where experts disagree.

quizzes.title: A City in Three Eras
quizzes.hook: Match clues from street life, buildings and trades to the right era of one invented city.
rounds: 4 clues: match transport clues to one of three eras
4 clues: match buildings and trades to eras
4 clues: choose what changed between eras and why
quizzes.seed: In an invented port city, match 'horse tram', 'grain elevator' and 'ferry dock' to Era 1, 2 or 3; several clues may share one era.
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 12 plus a three-era city strip showing your matches and the clue behind each.
quizzes.audience: City lovers and history fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Invented composite city inspired by general port-city patterns. Urban historian checks era plausibility; no real neighborhood claims; many-to-one matching needs partial credit.

quizzes.title: How a Word Crossed Borders
quizzes.hook: Trace how words travel between languages and learn which journeys are certain and which are still debated.
rounds: 5 words: match each to borrowed whole, translated piece by piece, or meaning shifted
3 routes: match words to the likely contact setting
quizzes.seed: Match each word to its journey: borrowed whole, translated piece by piece, or meaning shifted. Several words may share one journey type.
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus a route card marking certain versus debated word histories.
quizzes.audience: Language lovers and multilingual readers; Canada, Mexico, US; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Linguist review required. Skip contested etymologies or label them uncertain; no stereotypes about languages; French and Spanish editions need human adaptation.

quizzes.title: Book, Place, Era: Connect the Three
quizzes.hook: Link stories to the places and periods they depict, using the clues inside each passage.
rounds: 4 verified book titles: connect each to its stated setting
4 story periods: link each to the matching book, allowing shared periods
3 contrasts: distinguish depicted period from publication date
quizzes.seed: Connect The Great Gatsby to its stated setting and depicted decade, then distinguish that decade from its publication year.
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus a book-place-era map card listing the clues you used.
quizzes.audience: Readers and book clubs; Canada, Mexico, US; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Source setting, story period and publication date separately from authorized publisher/archive records; avoid invented excerpts that cannot uniquely identify a real region.

quizzes.title: Trade Routes Behind a Breakfast
quizzes.hook: Follow the ingredients on one plate back through the trade links that carried them.
rounds: 4 breakfast items: match each to a trade-link story
4 links: pick why an ingredient became common locally
quizzes.seed: Using a cited route map, connect an ingredient’s documented cultivation region, a named trade port and a dated destination.
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus a plate map showing multiple routes behind each item.

quizzes.production_note: Plant and trade histories have many contributors. quizzes.production_note: Invented sources. Historian confirms each relationship has a defensible reading; grant partial credit where a pair supports two readings.

quizzes.title: The Graphic Novel Workshop

quizzes.title: Time Capsule Packing Dilemma

quizzes.production_note: New preference scoring needed. Keep items culturally neutral; avoid ranking traditions; no claims about what any group would save. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Design the Local History Museum

quizzes.title: The Festival Calendar Has a Gap

quizzes.title: Pack the Pack Train

2 grids: choose the order of stops

quizzes.title: What the Railroad Changed

quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus a ripple chart separating documented effects from interpretation.

quizzes.title: Street Names: Clue or Overreach?

3 names: flag the overreach and pick a better source

quizzes.production_note: Street-name histories are often disputed. Use documented cases, label uncertainty, and check municipal archives; no folk-origin stories as answers.

quizzes.title: Made by Hand: Order the Steps

rounds: 3 sequences: order the steps of making paper
3 sequences: order the steps of making cloth
3 sequences: order the steps of setting type

quizzes.production_note: Craft historians review each sequence. Traditions of specific communities need community-authored sources and paid cultural review before inclusion.

quizzes.title: Living Cultures on the Museum Wall
quizzes.hook: Edit draft museum labels so they are accurate, current, and credit who should be telling the story.
rounds: 4 label drafts: choose wording that fits living communities
4 source choices: pick whose voice should author each label

quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus an editor's note on tense, authorship and named sources.

quizzes.production_note: Gate: paid Indigenous cultural review and community-authored sources before drafting. No tradition-specific facts without them; never frame communities as vanished. Specify a community and cited present-day source; multiple respectful phrasings can be valid.

quizzes.title: Many Hands Made This
quizzes.hook: Each player holds one clue; combine them to show a familiar tool had many contributors, not one inventor.

4 group timelines: agree on one order before the reveal

quizzes.audience: Friends, classrooms and families; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Pick topics with documented multiple contributors; historian review. Asynchronous play needs share-link support. Avoid dubious firsts and single-inventor claims.

quizzes.title: Letters Across the Border

Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices. Store and display knowledge accuracy separately from preference results.

quizzes.title: The Map Was Updated

2 maps: choose which legend change signals an update

quizzes.title: Soundscapes of Everyday Life
quizzes.hook: Listen to ordinary sounds from workplaces and homes and place them in time.
rounds: 4 original clips: identify the demonstrated mechanical action using a supplied device legend
4 dated archive cards: order documented device uses, not the sounds themselves
quizzes.seed: The supplied device legend identifies a typewriter bell and carriage return. Which mechanical action does the original clip demonstrate?
quizzes.payoff: Score out of 8 plus a sound timeline with transcripts of every clip.
quizzes.audience: Curious listeners and history fans; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Record original effects, no music or licensed samples. Transcripts and captions required; adoption dates need dated sources and gradual-adoption wording. A typewriter sound cannot date a recording or workplace. Tie historical chronology to explicit documented records.

quizzes.title: The Cropped Photograph
quizzes.hook: See how a crop changes an apparent historical story, then identify which claims the full frame actually supports.
rounds: 4 original or cleared images: choose the claim supported by the visible crop
4 full-frame reveals: revise the claim using added context

quizzes.payoff: Eight evidence decisions with paired crop/full-frame explanations.
quizzes.audience: Families and community archivists; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use original fictional scene illustrations or licensed archive photos with provenance; distinguish staged teaching scenes from historical evidence.

quizzes.title: Footnote Treasure Hunt
quizzes.hook: Follow a short trail of source cards to find which one actually supports a local-history claim.
rounds: 4 claims: select the supporting source card or insufficient-evidence option
3 footnote chains: order the path from claim to primary record
quizzes.seed: A brochure says the town was first, but its citation gives only an opening date. Which additional record would establish the comparison?
quizzes.payoff: Seven source-trail decisions with the exact missing evidence explained.
quizzes.audience: Local historians and students; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Use authored fictional source cards or cleared short excerpts. Closed-world evidence rules; no AI fact-checking or unsupported firstness claims.

quizzes.title: One Claim, Five Echoes
quizzes.hook: Five posts repeat one claim about an invented museum cafe. Trace who cited whom and count the observations that are really independent.

1 grid and 3 choices: what the log does and does not establish

quizzes.audience: Students, teachers and anyone who reads posts online; North America; globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Invented, harmless museum-cafe opening hours; not real news. Every post time, citation and independent observation is supplied, and the two graph tasks keep immediate citations and ultimate roots separate. Toy rules decide each answer. The NAMLE key questions page supports asking source and evidence questions; it does not give one right reading or show this quiz works. Do not copy NAMLE wording. Distinct from Fact Source Claim Interpretation and Cropped Photograph.

quizzes.title: Build a Home Cafe

quizzes.audience: Home-drink fans and cafe daydreamers; North America, globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Write original, price-free options; check every option maps to both dimensions; no drink-health claims; do not reuse report wording. Requires new preference scoring; never use correct/incorrect credit for taste choices.

quizzes.title: Kitchen Tool Detective
quizzes.hook: Read the evidence left on a board or plate and name the tool that most plausibly did it.

quizzes.payoff: Detective rank from raw score out of 8, with a one-line tool explanation per case.
quizzes.audience: Curious home cooks and gadget-drawer owners; North America, globally playable
quizzes.production_note: Each answer needs a cooking-reference citation and an editor check that no second suspect is equally plausible.

quizzes.title: Flavor Triangle

quizzes.audience: Everyday cooks and taste-curious eaters; North America, globally playable

quizzes.title: Fridge-to-Meal Puzzle

2 repair choices: identify the one change that resolves a contradiction

quizzes.production_note: Record original clips; supply transcripts and captions; drop ambiguous sounds; reviewer confirms each answer; needs new audio player control. Avoid oil-temperature, cooking-readiness or safety inferences from audio; provide an equivalent written stimulus.
